turns.content: For a positive integer n, order floor(n^(1/8)), floor(n^(1/7)), ..., floor(n^(1/2)). If all seven values are distinct, what minimum spacing between successive integer values follows?

Let b=floor(n^(1/8)). Translate that spacing into lower bounds b,b+1,...,b+6 for the eighth- through second-root floors, and convert them into power lower bounds for n. Also record the upper bound implied by floor(n^(1/8))=b.
Write the joint lower threshold as the maximum of b^8,(b+1)^7,(b+2)^6,(b+3)^5,(b+4)^4,(b+5)^3,(b+6)^2. Explain why satisfying only one of these bounds would be insufficient.

For b=1, replace only the sixth-root-floor rung b+2 by b+1 while retaining the rest of the ladder. Compare the eighth-root upper bound with the strongest lower bound under this modified ladder and decide whether the case is feasible.
Analyze b=2 by evaluating all seven power bounds and taking their maximum. What is the least candidate n in this case, and does it respect the eighth-root upper bound?
Show that every case b>=3 has n>=3^8 and therefore cannot improve on the candidate from b=2.
Directly compute the floors of the square through eighth roots of the candidate, and check that n itself is distinct from all of them.
State the smallest positive integer n and list the eight distinct quantities in the order requested.
